fact: The Chief Justice of Nigeria launched the Nigerian Case Management System at the Supreme Court on 1 July 2026, with phase one requiring counsel to upload electronic copies of processes and records for pending appeals set for hearing September to December 2026.

The Chief Justice said the NCMS will expand quarterly until all pending Supreme Court appeals are captured, and the Judicial Information Technology Policy Committee chairman said it is designed to link High Courts, the National Industrial Court and the Sharia and Customary Courts of Appeal to the Court of Appeal and Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court's 2026 practice directions, in force from 1 July 2026, require counsel to upload electronic copies of processes and records of appeal to the NCMS, starting with appeals set for hearing from September 2026.

Judicial IT Policy Committee chair Kashim Zannah said Borno, Bayelsa, Delta, Niger and Taraba state judiciaries had already adopted similar electronic systems, and that Borno's court documents were kept safe in the cloud through the 2024 Maiduguri flood.

Federal High Court Chief Judge John Tsoho said the court launched its electronic filing system in the Lagos Division, where litigants can file from any location with internet access and fees go through integrated gateways.

Taraba Chief Judge Joel Agya said the state's high courts have keyed into the Nigeria Case Management System, legal mail and e-filing application, with a pilot to digitise proceedings starting in the Chief Judge's court and staff trained.

The Nigerian Case Management System was introduced at the Supreme Court in 2012 and, per the Chief Justice in the 2025/2026 legal year, is being progressively adopted as an official nationwide platform developed under the National Judicial Council.

The Chief Justice says all backlog cases in the High Courts are being uploaded into the NCMS, and the Supreme Court is moving to e-filing integrated with it, with a module still being developed and no launch date.
The Federal High Court said manual filing of new cases in its Lagos Division ends April 24 and the e-filing platform becomes operational from April 27, with all new filings exclusively electronic.
